overall: The Board violated the Open Meeting Law by failing to periodically review executive session minutes for release or to announce and record the results; the AG declined the remaining allegations.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly convened in executive session on April 23 without first announcing the purpose for the executive session.
allegations.key_passage: The Board’s failure to announce the purposes for convening in executive session was reasonably discoverable on April 23; therefore, we decline to review this allegation where the complaint was not filed with the Board until 82 days after the alleged violation was reasonably discoverable.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly has not timely approved its executive session minutes.
allegations.key_passage: That executive session minutes are not required to be “approved” in a timely manner does not leave their creation to the whim of the public body.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly does not re-evaluate executive session minutes after 30 days for release.
allegations.key_passage: Instead, it requires that a public body review at reasonable intervals its executive session minutes to determine if they must be released to the public.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to periodically review executive session minutes for release and to announce the results of any review.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, we find that the Board either failed to periodically review its executive session minutes to determine if they must be released to the public or failed to announce and record the results of such a review.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to respond to multiple requests, made 2022 to 2025, for executive session minutes and is withholding evidence tied to litigation.
allegations.key_passage: We decline to review this allegation where the complaint does not identify any specific request for meeting minutes to which it is alleged the Board failed to respond.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to provide records other than meeting minutes requested by the complainant.
allegations.key_passage: we decline to review this allegation as well where requests for records other than meeting minutes fall under the Public Records Law, not the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Board allegedly failed to inform the public of matters related to the complainant's lawsuit against the Town.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not require that a public body discuss any particular matter nor that it discuss a matter in any particular depth.

allegations.summary: Town Administrator allegedly violated the Open Meeting Law.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not apply to individual municipal officials, such as the Town Administrator

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, with a caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law.

Within 60 days, review all executive session minutes it continues to withhold to determine whether the purposes remain ongoing or have been served, announce the results at its next open session, and record them in the minutes.
remedy_passage: We order the Board’s immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law and caution that similar future violations may be considered evidence of an intent to violate the Law. We additionally order that within 60 days of the date of this letter the Board review all executive session minutes it continues to withhold to determine whether the executive session purposes remain ongoing or whether the purposes have been served and the minutes must be released to the public.
